correctness.rationale: PASS: For ordered nine-eigenvalue spectra the APPT necessary outer inequality is lambda1≤lambda7+lambda8+lambda9. In difference coordinates its cone has six positive rays, one zero, two negative, yielding exactly 15 vertices (3 surviving plus 12 crossings), not merely an assumed numerical list. Exact Fraction enumeration reproduces unique outer maximum 25/169 at (3,3,1^7)/13, second vertex value 11/75, gamma=16/12675, q0=16/845 and D²=58/1183. The first Hildebrand qutrit matrix at the maximizer has a strictly negative eigenvalue (2−2sqrt2)/13; the Frobenius-Lipschitz bound ||K(lambda)-K(star)||F≤2||lambda-star|| yields t≥t0=7(sqrt2−1)/sqrt406. In a vertex decomposition, G=Fstar−F(lambda)≥max(gamma*t, q0*t−D²*t²). Endpoint comparisons for t∈[t0,t*] and linear bound for t≥t*, t*=784/2175, give G≥12544/27568125. The complete exact-vertex verifier was read; the new independent rational arithmetic reproduces all constants. Uses the qutrit PSD matrix only as a necessary APPT condition, not an equivalence.

value.rationale: PASS, modest but substantive: The exact two-qutrit APPT maximum is open; prior outer-polytope bound was known to be strictly unattainable but without an explicit rational separation. A rigorously checkable positive rational gap quantifies that separation for a natural fixed physical dimension and gives a concrete obstruction to approaching its unique outer candidate. It is nonsharp and not advertised as an optimization solution, so its mathematical utility is the first explicit quantitative certificate rather than the tiny numerical gain alone.

final_claim: Every absolutely-PPT state on C^3⊗C^3 has purity at most 312737/2120625 = 25/169−12544/27568125; the displayed positive gap improves the known strict outer-polytope purity inequality and is not claimed sharp.
limitations: Not an exact maximum; fixed two-qutrit dimension and only necessary one-matrix APPT condition.
Quantitative gap is small and other Hildebrand matrices might allow much stronger bounds.
